open-question.question: The recorded decisions fix the one-liner word for word but describe the new bold README tagline only by intent (it keeps the cairn trail-marker image and says the path is marked before the walk, so the walk can be handed off, without repeating the one-liner). What is the exact wording of the tagline that replaces "Mark the path from idea to shipped."?

The decisions set all four GitHub repository descriptions and the root repository topics with gh inside the milestone, and say the root README goes live when it is pushed, but they do not say who pushes or when, and the local main branch is currently ahead of origin by unpushed commits. Does the milestone itself push main to GitHub so the new README appears together with the new descriptions and topics, or is the push left to the maintainer outside the milestone, with the descriptions and topics allowed to run ahead of the published README?

alternative.id: Push inside the milestone with the gh edits

open-question.alternative: The milestone pushes main itself. The task that sets the four GitHub repository descriptions and the root repository topics with gh first pushes main to origin, and that push carries the already-committed root README rewrite. It then makes the gh edits in the same task, so the new README, descriptions, and topics go public together. The README task has to be ordered before this task, because a task's own changes are committed only after it finishes. The push is a plain fast-forward and is never forced. It closes the gap the question names. The root repository page never shows a new-identity description and topics above the old "Mark the path from idea to shipped." README, and the one remaining mismatch is the distribution repositories. The recorded rollout decision already accepts that one until the next release. A task completion would make a push to the shared public remote that cannot be undone, and no runner does that today: only /release-plugin pushes main. Under complete-all-tasks the push would happen unattended inside a dispatched agent. It would publish all of the milestone's unpushed commits mid-milestone, 39 of them at the moment, while TASKS_TODO.md still lists open work. A failed push (credentials or a non-fast-forward) would fail the task halfway through.

No task pushes main. The requirements record that pushing is the maintainer's own act, done outside the milestone whenever they choose, for example right after finishing it. The gh edits to the descriptions and topics happen inside the milestone as already decided. Until that push the root repository's description and topics run ahead of its published README. Pushing to the public remote stays a deliberate human act, matching how the project works now: no skill or task pushes except the release, and origin/main is pushed by hand between releases (its tip is today's Readme-adoption commit). Task completion stays local and reversible until the maintainer looks over the finished milestone. The public root repository shows a mismatched identity for as long as the push waits: the new one-liner and topics at the top, and the old tagline and milestone-driven one-liner in the README beneath them. Nothing in the milestone bounds that window, so it lasts until the maintainer remembers to push.

alternative.id: Root README goes live with the next release

open-question.alternative: No task pushes main, and main is deliberately not pushed until the next ordinary /release-plugin run. That run already pushes main (its step 8a) before it publishes the distribution trees. The root README then goes live at the same moment as the rebuilt host READMEs and manifests. The gh edits to the descriptions and topics still happen inside the milestone as already decided, so all four run ahead of their READMEs until that release. Every file-based pitch surface (the root README, the three host READMEs, and the five manifest description strings) switches to the new identity in one release instead of two separate moments. The push needs no new runner behaviour, because the release skill's existing push-main step does it. The mismatch on the root repository lasts longest under this option: from the gh edits until a release that the milestone does not schedule. It also asks the maintainer to hold back their usual pushes between releases, and any unrelated push in the meantime would publish the README early anyway.
